name: Centro de Procesamiento de Datos del Gobierno de Cantabria

profile.reading: This is the Centro de Proceso de Datos, or Data Processing Center, of the regional Government of Cantabria, in Santander, Spain, though no source found this session discloses a specific street address for the building. The center sustains the majority of the Cantabrian regional governments information and communications technology and e-administration services, supporting roughly 6,000 machines across the government, including about 4,600 desktop computers, 400 laptops, and 800 servers, serving more than 5,600 users spread across roughly 200 government facilities and offices, and operates under the General Directorate of Organization and Technology within the Department of the Presidency and Justice. The center was substantially modernized under a regional program called Osiris, financed in part through European Union FEDER structural funds, with total planned investment of about 32 million euros over a four year period running through 2020; as of an April 2018 site visit documented by a regional engineering association, roughly 14 million euros of that investment had already been spent on infrastructure and deployment. This government run internal data center is distinct from a separately announced first public and private use data center for Cantabria, a newer commercial facing infrastructure project the regional government said would enter service in 2024, which this registry treats as a different project rather than conflating the two. The Osiris programs planned four year investment window ran through 2020, marking the rough completion point of this modernization effort, though this reflects the programs funding timeline rather than necessarily a single specific building construction date for the underlying data processing center itself, a distinction this registry notes honestly.
